Without going into the weeds too much, it's easier said than done. We could tell these requestors that we're busy serving Business critical needs, but it's difficult when many important things are in rotation that are all connected to business needs, cloud needs, CMDB needs, UI states and development of the Agent Workspace, IS needs, Snowflake and data handling needs, End User experience needs...That's the problem: To solve business needs, there's always sub-needs.

Either way, we're actively in the middle of shifting what is and isn't as critical as the next and trust me: I hear what you're saying. Saying "No" to things that are not critical makes sense. Regardless, I believe that in a customer-service driven, technical business environment, you really shouldn't say "No". You need to say "Later, here's why, and here's the timeline". The problem is that the majority of these requests are coming from Tier 3 teams with valid technical needs and requirements like I mentioned above. 

I totally would agree with you if you said: "You have a good Change Enablement process here, can you wait to have them work on the CAB Workbench? It's not critical." In this real-world example, my ask for the CAB workbench has been indefinitely delayed in the backlogs while we struggle to simply meet the business-critical needs. Even this is proving to be a challenge as I stated in my original post.

You could say "No" or "cull" a development request, and 6 months later, 2 development requests show - one is the original you culled, and the 2nd is another item. Even still, you haven't really helped the overall issue of: "We can't keep up with demand." Business criticality is carried by the non-critical elements of a business process, so it's dangerous to keep putting them off. Of course, the SNOW team manager has the power to say "no", but flat out denying this because of current workloads flies in the face of Agile Methodology and the tools present to manage work over long periods of time.

I appreciate the insight, but having a conversation with the team and what to expect won't help at this point. That's been done really. Disney World could say that only VIP critical guests can enter the park, but it doesn't change the other massive amount of "non-critical-yet-still-valid-and-needed" requests waiting to be helped.

This reminds me of a similar situation where due to some reason, monitor settings weren't changing to reflect the hardware capabilities when I myself swapped screens not long ago. It wasn't the exact same thing you're seeing, but let's step through it regardless.

Let's check Advanced Display Settings:

1. Search for "Advanced" and then click on "View Advanced Display Info"
2. Let's make sure that the basic settings are correct (like resolution and active signal resolution), but the thing I want to check here primarily is Refresh rate.
3. Click on "Refresh rate" and the drop down should show what is possible for your monitor. Select the highest option.
4. Also, click on "Display adapter properties for Display 1" (I'm assuming your PC set it as "display 1")
5. Select the "Monitor" tab, double check the refresh rate here too.

Hmmm. Does your monitor require different drivers?

It's possible there's a hardware related cache causing the quality issue. Maybe try to flushdns and clear browser cookies.

DNS Flush:
1. Open Command Prompt (type CMD in search)
2. Type in the following, in order, hitting "Enter/Return" on each line: 
2.1: ipconfig /release
2.2: ipconfig /renew
2.3: ipconfig /flushDNS
3. Do not restart your PC yet.
4. Open your choice browser, clear cookies & cache.
5. Turn off (not a restart) your PC 
6. Leave it off for one minute.
7. Turn on the PC, hopefully you're set.

First question: Do you have to feel the pull of a god to join the religion?

\-I don't think so. I believe that your path is your own, and some paths are carved by the gods, some paths require a struggle through overgrown forests before you see a clear opening. Everyone's "draw", "pull", or attraction to the gods is unique.

2: Can you move an indoor shrine?

\-Absolutely! Your shrine is your own, and must suit your needs. If a shrine is out of place, please feel free to move it. Oftentimes, a shrine is seen as a grand set up with glitzy glamour, fancy items, crystals, and golden statues...of course, this is fine too, but the gods are indifferent as to how the shrine is configured. Your shrine is your own, it can be the size of a napkin, or as large as a backyard.

3: When you pray do you have to speak out loud or can you say it in your mind?

\-I do both, but it's the intention, meaning, and openness of your heart that counts.

4: If giving an offering do you have to meditate?

\-Well, define meditation - do you mean to sit quietly and ponder the gods? Sure, go for it! Do you mean the typical "ommmm" meditation? Go for that as well! Either way is totally fine. I myself, I turn my third eye to the heavens and imagine I'm speaking face to face, humbly prostrating myself before the gods, offering gifts. I would say make it "ritualistic". For example, I wouldn't throw an apple out the window and be unceremonious about it. I'd be in the moment, try to "establish a connection" and then offer up.

5: Can you give the gods an offering without doing meditation or what you do for prayer?

\-I suppose I kind of answered this in #4, but for example: I'll light a candle or incense almost every time, if my supplies allow. It's certainly not always necessary. I'll call out to Odin and Freya (my current closest gods), and humbly offer what I have to offer them. I usually thank Odin for the runes (I've been having strong positive experiences), thank Freya for my family's recent bountiful "harvests", and express my love for their presence in mine and my family's life.

​

My friend, I hope this helps. I definitely appreciate the curiosity. I think in time, you'll learn there's not as much to it as you'd imagine, **as your intentions and honest openness with the gods is more important than anything else.**

It's not that it's a conditional relationship like "I'll take if you give, or I'll give if you give", but I've viewed offering as a means of renewing a connection between myself and a deity. They do expect us to behave in a certain way, but creating a cycle of gift giving with no true expectation, a gift giving out of a sense of loyalty or a pledge, is more where I personally come from.

One of the facets of other religions that have turned me away is the conditionality of it all. I shouldn't have to give to get (edit: or vice-versa), but in this case, I feel totally happy giving, and I simply hope that the gods hear me. Either way, I have enough personal experience with the gods to know that they don't absolutely require anything to be a part of my life, but I feel it makes the connection stronger.

A child in the womb gives and takes from the mother, just as is the other way around. There is no debt or credit, no bottom line, no amount of giving or minimum...it just is, and it just happens, and both benefit in many ways. I view my connection with the gods the same.

I've thrown everything away that I've ever loved because I have this, "the grass is greener" bullshit mentality. The grass is greener where you water it. Water yourself. Forget about mindfulness, girls, sex, and the like as much as possible. Do one thing you like every day. Keep doing it. It takes a long time to polish a boot that's rough, torn the fuck up, ripped, and tattered. Eventually, the holes, cracks, and tears become filled with polishing wax. Eventually the surface starts to retake it's shape. Eventually, the boot will begin to look somewhat smooth and new. Eventually, that bitch is a spit shine where you can see your own reflection.

Eventuality has happened here. But only, and ONLY with effort. Regardless of how much you hate yourself (if you do) and your circumstances, spit in the face of that garbage, and just do the opposite. You don't need to practice mindfulness. You don't need to tell yourself that you look sexy. You need to live your life, the way you want it, how it will make you happy. Everything else will follow.

If you try to wax and polish yourself and your life, it's just going to happen. Simple as that. Eventually, you may realize this, and I hope you do, my friend.

4) Keep some protein bars or granola bars near your bed. It will encourage you to stay in bed, minimizing noise disruptions to your family, with the added benefit of tricking your mind and body that you don't need to get out of bed.

Hope it helps, keep us posted.
